title: Random-forest screening identifies experimentally active anti-CRISPR families
summary: A learned model ranked candidate protein families for experimental follow-up. Testing supported two previously unknown anti-CRISPR proteins in the studied system. The much larger predicted family catalog remains computational and is not counted as experimentally validated discoveries. Assay activity does not establish native-host function or improved genome-editing performance.
ai_technology: Extremely randomized forest of genomic-context features
organization: National Institutes of Health; University of California, San Francisco

evidence.tested: Selected predicted candidates received functional laboratory tests.
evidence.unknown: Broader family validation, native-host activity and practical utility remain unestablished.
evidence.ai_role: Extremely randomized forest of genomic-context features supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary published PDF abstract, affiliations and model-training Methods; experimental scope checked against prior primary review.
